column1: # Game profile of Batman: Arkham Asylum (Switch, update 1.0.1 = v65536, over the 6.84 GB base game). Playable on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file
# Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 (package version 0x243, licensee 0x15) with FMOD, Bink movies and Scaleform menus, SDK 14.3.0 (the sdk build of Batman: Arkham Knight 1.0.5, 2aef2cff…).
# The shaders are compact records in the global shader cache (GlobalShaderCache-Switch.bin) and in the Oodle packages (*.xxx): the loader main+0xcc6194 builds each control section from
# a fixed template and the record's metadata (shader_split.py ue3_compact): 31,263 of them
# The NPDM declares no system resource (no virtual address memory): main sets a heap, of at most the pool − 64 MB (the survey's guess, a 3328 MB heap region)
# The game selects near-zero NVN depth (one nvnDeviceSetDepthMode call at boot); offline pipeline bases use main0_z.
# 60 fps: the game asks for present interval 2, and the engine caps itself at 30 (Coalesced_<language>.bin: bSmoothFrameRate, MaxSmoothedFrameRate=30). With the configurations'
# MaxSmoothedFrameRate at 60 (a RomFS overlay, README.md Frame rate) and one frame per display tick here, it runs at 60; Unreal Engine 3 steps by the time that passed (walking
# for 3 s covers the same ground at 30 and 60 fps). Without the overlay the engine's own cap keeps it at 30
